children: The U.K. housing market is grinding along rather than powering ahead, RBC Capital Markets analysts Anthony Codling and Oliver Dyson say in a note. According to the Nationwide House Price Index for August, annual prices grew 1.6% with a modest 0.2% month-on-month uptick, RBC says. On a non-seasonally adjusted basis the average U.K. home now costs 275,465 pounds, below July's 276,581 pounds, thus underlining just how flat conditions really are, RBC says. Geopolitical tensions are keeping energy prices and market interest rates elevated and cast a shadow over consumer confidence and mortgage affordability, the analysts say. Although wage growth continues to outpace house-price growth, so affordability is improving gradually, higher mortgage rates are eating into those gains, the analysts say. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)
